Charge control needs support from your device’s ROM, and a permission that apps cannot grant themselves. You set it up by hand.

Currently: Pixel 6a or newer phones on Android 15+, Samsung on verified One UI versions, Xiaomi on HyperOS 2, and OnePlus, Oppo, or Realme on ColorOS 15. Amply checks your exact device and shows what works.
You grant the permission yourself: with one ADB command from a computer, or through the Shizuku app. Some devices require Shizuku. The dashboard walks you through the right option.

Amply needs one durable Android permission to change the charge policy.

With Shizuku, Amply can confirm the configured policy and run diagnostics, not just write it. Start or install Shizuku and allow Amply; the durable permission is then granted automatically. The button below is a manual fallback if that fails.
Easiest: no ADB install needed. On the computer your phone is plugged into, open this link in Chrome or Edge to grant control over USB. Shizuku is still needed for diagnostics and reliable readback.

Amply detects the permission automatically once it runs, or tap Refresh in the top bar.
Does the limit actually work here?

Your phone accepts a charge limit, but on some builds nothing behind it ever stops the charging. Amply can\'t tell the difference just by watching: a battery resting below the limit looks exactly like one paused by heat or a weak charger.

This check settles it. Amply sets a limit below your current level and waits for charging to stop, raises the limit and waits for it to start again, then lowers it once more. Nothing but a real, working limit does that on command. Leave the charger connected throughout. It usually takes 30 to 90 minutes.
Your own charge setting is put back at the end, and also if you stop the check, unplug, or the phone restarts partway through.
Amply will set the limit to %1$d%% first, which is below where your battery is now, so charging should stop almost immediately.

The limit does not work here

Your phone accepted the limit and charged straight past it, so nothing behind the setting is stopping the charging. Amply has switched its charging controls off here rather than show a protection that isn\'t real. Sending the result helps get this build looked at.
Charging never stopped after the limit was set, but it also never went past the limit, so this isn\'t proof either way — a slow charger can look the same. Nothing was recorded. You can try again.

Charging stopped, but it didn\'t start again when the limit was raised. That can mean a full battery, a weak charger, or a warm phone rather than a broken limit, so nothing was recorded. Try again with a different charger or a cooler phone.
Charging stopped and started again, but didn\'t stop the second time. Nothing was recorded. You can try again.

Your phone did stop charging, but at a different level than Amply asked for, which means the setting means something else on this build. Nothing was recorded. Sending the result is genuinely useful — it says exactly what the setting does here.
Amply couldn\'t read anything reliable about how much charge was going in on this phone, so it can\'t judge the result. Nothing was recorded.

Your battery filled up during the check. A full battery stops charging on its own, so from here on Amply can\'t tell that apart from the limit working. Nothing was recorded. Try again from a lower battery level.
The battery didn\'t reach the limit in time. Nothing was recorded. A faster charger would help.

Too little charge was going into your phone for the check to have anything to compare against — a weak charger, a nearly full battery, or a phone that doesn\'t report its charge accurately. Nothing was recorded. Try again with a different charger from a lower battery level.
The check never got started. Nothing was recorded.

Your phone reports how much charge is going in too rarely for this check. With updates that far apart, charging that never stopped and charging that stopped on command look the same, so Amply won\'t call it either way. Nothing was recorded.

Your phone stopped reporting the charger as connected while Amply had the lower limit set. Some builds report it that way when the limit engages, and it looks the same if the cable slipped out. Amply can\'t tell those apart, so it can\'t finish the check. Make sure the cable is firmly connected and try again. How full the battery is, as a percentage. It is the phone\'s own estimate rather than a direct measurement, so it can move in jumps when the estimate is corrected.

How fast energy is going into the battery, measured at the battery itself (voltage x current). It is normally highest early in a charge and tapers off near the top. It is only recorded while the battery is actually taking charge.
The battery cell voltage. It rises as the battery fills and drops under load, so it tracks the charge level rather than the charging speed.
The current flowing in or out of the battery. Positive normally means charging and negative means discharging, but the sign is up to the manufacturer, so some devices report it the other way round.
The battery temperature reported by the phone. Sustained heat is what ages a battery fastest, so a charge that stays cool is easier on it than a fast one that runs hot.

resources.string: Amply needs to record a few more charges before it can estimate how long yours take.
Protect your battery in system settings
Samsung phones include battery protection under Settings → Battery → Battery protection. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can turn it on there.
OnePlus and Oppo phones offer charge limiting under Settings → Battery → Battery health (or Smart charging). Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can enable it there.
Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO phones may offer charge limiting or protection under Settings → Battery → Battery protection. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can look for it there.
Look for charging optimization under Settings → Battery. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device.
LineageOS includes Charging control under Settings → Battery. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but you can set a limit there.
Your phone may offer a built-in battery-protection or charge-limit option in its battery settings. Amply can\'t control it directly on this device, but it\'s worth a look.
